skill.name: orchestration
skill.description: Guide for orchestrating Claude Code tasks across Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and other external AI CLIs using native Task agents.
skill.summary: Guide Claude Code users through multi-provider CLI delegation, read-only defaults, worktree isolation, auth recovery, and result collection.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and path traversal alerts are Markdown documentation artifacts, not executable code in the skill. The remaining risk is material because the guide recommends broad external CLI permissions, provider delegation, and write-mode commands that can transmit context or modify repositories.

remediation.issue: Broad wildcard Bash permissions for external AI CLIs.
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard allow rules with narrow command patterns and require confirmation before enabling each provider.

remediation.issue: External provider delegation can disclose user prompts or repository context.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, redaction, and data-handling guidance before any prompt is sent to Codex, Gemini, Cursor, or another provider.

remediation.issue: Write-mode examples use workspace-write, --yolo, and --force flags.
remediation.suggestion: Keep read-only mode as the default and require explicit approval plus worktree isolation for any write-mode execution.

content.value_statement: Multi-provider AI workflows can be hard to run consistently and safely. This skill gives Claude Code users a repeatable guide for delegating work to external AI CLIs.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to choose Codex, Gemini, or Cursor for delegated coding tasks.
Documents read-only and write-mode command patterns for supported AI CLIs.
Provides a workflow for launching native Task agents and collecting TaskOutput results.
Describes authentication recovery with fork-terminal fallback when a CLI login is needed.
Recommends git worktree isolation for write-mode agent work.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not a bundled automation script.
It depends on locally installed and authenticated external AI CLIs.
It can expose prompts or repository context to external providers if used carelessly.
Write-mode examples require careful review before changes are merged.

use_cases.title: Delegate Code Review
use_cases.description: Send a read-only review task to Codex or Gemini and collect the returned findings.

use_cases.title: Compare Provider Responses
use_cases.description: Run the same analysis prompt across multiple AI CLIs to compare coverage and recommendations.

use_cases.title: Isolate Agent Edits
use_cases.description: Use a separate git worktree before allowing an external agent to make code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Read-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the orchestration guidance to run a read-only Codex review of the current change. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex and Gemini in read-only mode to analyze this bug. Return a short comparison of their findings.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Isolated Edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a worktree-isolated write-mode task for Cursor. Include the review steps before any merge.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From Auth Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Follow the auth recovery workflow for a failed Gemini invocation, then retry the original read-only prompt.

output_examples.input: Ask Codex to review a pending change without editing files.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects Codex, uses read-only mode, launches a background Task agent, and returns a concise review summary.

output_examples.input: Run the same architecture question through Codex and Gemini.
output_examples.output: The assistant starts both providers, collects their results, and compares agreement, conflicts, and remaining questions.

output_examples.input: Let Cursor propose edits for a refactor.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a separate worktree, records the intended scope, and asks for review before merging changes.

best_practices: Use read-only mode unless the user explicitly approves write access.
Review provider output and local diffs before accepting any agent-generated changes.
Use separate worktrees for parallel or experimental write-mode tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not grant wildcard CLI permissions without understanding the commands they allow.
Do not send secrets, proprietary code, or private data to external providers without approval.
Do not merge agent-written changes before inspecting the diff and test results.

faq.question: Does this skill run external AI tools by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents how Claude Code can invoke external AI CLIs through native Task agents.

faq.question: Which providers are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers Codex, Gemini, and Cursor command patterns, with related orchestration references.

faq.question: Can it keep agents from editing files?
faq.answer: It recommends read-only defaults and provider flags, but local configuration must enforce those limits.

faq.question: When should I use worktree isolation?
faq.answer: Use it for write-mode tasks, experimental changes, multi-file refactors, and parallel agent work.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication failures?
faq.answer: It describes a fork-terminal fallback for interactive login, then retrying the native invocation.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is broad external CLI access that may send context to providers or modify files.
